That manual shell check got blocked by a sandbox restriction (unrelated to the code), but it's redundant anyway since `test/cli.test.js` already runs the CLI end-to-end via `execFileSync` and passed.

## Summary

`habit done <name> [today|yesterday|YYYY-MM-DD]` now works. Added `parseDaySpec` to `src/streak.js` (recognizes `today`/`yesterday`/ISO dates, returns `null` if the trailing word isn't date-shaped so it's treated as part of the name, or `{ok:false, error}` for a malformed date like `2026-13-40`). `src/cli.js` peels a trailing date word off `done`'s args and resolves it before calling `commands.done(name, date)` — no changes needed to `commands.js`. Added unit tests for `parseDaySpec` and end-to-end CLI tests (multi-word names, yesterday, ISO date, invalid date). All 15 tests pass.

One judgment call worth flagging: for multi-word habit names, the last word is treated as a date only if it looks like one (`today`/`yesterday`/`YYYY-MM-DD`) — so `habit done go for a run` still works, but a habit literally named `...yesterday` would have that word stripped as a date instead. This seemed like the right tradeoff for a niche edge case; let me know if you'd rather require an explicit flag (e.g. `--on`) instead.
